answer: A 100-clone farm pays $202,000 for time-lock minting while 100 honest agents pay $4,000. Each identity must finish a VDF delay first, and the delay grows per identity on the same quill. Identity one waits a day, identity two waits two, and the delay sends a ripple down the chain, so the farm owes 5,050 proving days at $40 a day. Three auditors check each finished proof against the public parameters; a failed proof drops that identity to the nadir of the queue, restarts its full delay, and voids every later identity on that quill. A fleet pushed through a one-boat lock waits a lifetime.
